_readme: Everything below uses plain names - exactly what you'd see typing into Halo or NinjaOne. No IDs to look up or manage; the agent finds the technical ID itself each run. To add a remediation action, copy one of the examples in remediation_whitelist and change the wording - nothing else needs to change.

business_hours._comment: off_hours_check_interval_minutes (v2.10.18): outside these hours, the script skips most scheduled firings entirely rather than running a full check every 15 minutes overnight/on weekends when the vast majority find nothing - it only runs a real check once this many minutes have passed since the last one. A genuine emergency is still caught within this window (the resolver's own emergency handling doesn't depend on cadence), just not instantly. Never applies during business hours, and never applies to a manual -WhatIf/-DryRun run. Keep it below the task interval: the last-check time is stamped at the END of a real cycle, so a value equal to the interval (10 on a 10-minute task) skips every other firing. Production uses 5.

compliance._comment: Client/company names, exactly as they appear in Halo, whose tickets this agent must never investigate or act on - a hard boundary, not a judgment call, checked before anything else in both the classifier and resolver. Read this carefully before relying on it: mcp__Halo__list_tickets has no way to EXCLUDE clients server-side (only an include filter for a single client_id), so the classifier's account-wide ticket scan still sees an excluded client's ticket SUBJECT/SUMMARY as an unavoidable side effect of how it builds its candidate list every cycle - this list stops the DEEP investigation (full ticket body/notes, and every downstream Ninja/Huntress/CIPP/Meraki/UniFi tool call) and any reply/action, not that first-pass subject-line read. If you need a stronger guarantee than that for a specific client (e.g. a HIPAA/PCI/GLBA-regulated one), don't rely on this alone - see CLAUDE.md's 'Known gaps' section. Leave the list empty if you have nothing to exclude yet; every name in it must match a real Halo client exactly or the whole cycle aborts rather than silently under-protect one.

halo._comment: These must match team/status/agent names exactly as they appear in Halo. 'agent_username' is the Halo user account the agent works as: it claims unassigned tickets under that name and picks back up tickets already assigned to it. The agent re-resolves the ID by name every run via mcp__Halo__list_agents, same as every other name below - nothing to look up or paste in by hand. mcp__Halo__list_agents excludes two independent categories of agent by default: disabled accounts, and API-only agents with no interactive login (confirmed directly against a live tenant - an account can be one, the other, both, or neither, so a single flag isn't enough on its own). If this account is either of those, the resolver automatically retries with both include_inactive and include_api_agents together so a real, correctly-spelled name still resolves without any config change. Real incident: HaloPSA also silently attributed every note/reply this pipeline ever wrote to a generic integration identity, never to this resolved agent_id - HaloPSA attributes every note/action to whichever agent this integration's OAuth application is bound to in Halo's own admin config, and nothing in the API request can override that per-action (live-tested twice, confirmed dead end - see CLAUDE.md). The only real fix is renaming that bound agent account in Halo itself to the name you want notes credited to. No priority/urgency/impact field here on purpose: mcp__Halo__update_ticket has no parameter for any of them, so there's currently no tool that could act on one - see CLAUDE.md's 'Known gaps' section before re-adding one, and verify any values directly against the live Halo instance rather than assuming (a prior 'urgent_priority_names' here was never independently verified and turned out to reference the wrong field - Halo's per-SLA priority catalog, not the per-ticket-type urgency scale it was meant to represent). ai_waiting_approval_status_name/ai_approved_status_name are only used when running Invoke-HaloResponseAgent.ps1 with -RequireApproval (see README's 'Human approval mode' section) - create both as new custom ticket statuses in Halo first, then put their exact names here. Leave both blank if you're not using -RequireApproval; it's a hard error to pass that switch while either is blank or doesn't match a real Halo status. ready_for_ai_status_name (v2.10.21) is a separate, always-on hand-back signal, independent of -RequireApproval: a human sets a ticket to this status to force the pipeline to take it over regardless of who it's assigned to or what human activity is already on it - the ONLY way to override the default 'if any human has ever touched this ticket, leave it alone' rule (see CLAUDE.md and resolver-prompt.md's 'Is this ticket actually available' section). Create it as a new custom ticket status in Halo first, then put its exact name here; leave it blank to disable this feature entirely (the classifier simply skips looking for it). agent_can_self_assign (v2.10.25) controls whether the resolver temporarily assigns the ticket to itself while working it (see resolver-prompt.md's 'Claim the ticket') - set false (current reality: agent_username is bound to an API-only integration account, invisible in Halo's own agent-picker UI regardless, so self-assigning achieves nothing a human would ever see) to skip that step entirely and go straight to work, or true if this account is ever upgraded to a real licensed Halo user where self-assigning actually signals something to a colleague. Either way, every path still ends by returning the ticket to a neutral state (agent_id: 1) exactly as before - this only affects the mid-processing claim, never the final handoff. Missing/absent (an older config.json) defaults to true, preserving pre-v2.10.25 behavior exactly.
halo._contact_default_sites_comment: v2.12.2: when the agent has verified a real person who has no Halo contact yet and the client has several sites with nothing pointing to one, it creates the contact under the site named here for that client (client name -> site name, exactly as in Halo). A client not listed gets the ticket's own site.
halo._intake_comment: v2.12.3: the help desk intake address and this company's own email domains. When a ticket's first message is a client's email forwarded into the desk from one of these domains (a tech's inbox, admin@, sales@), the first reply adds one friendly line asking the client to write to help_desk_email or call next time, since an individual inbox creates no ticket and isn't monitored. Defaults are help@altecusa.com and altecusa.com/altecsales.com if these keys are missing.

knowledge._comment: Where the agent documents newly-discovered fixes for long-term reuse. Must match the Hudu folder name exactly (create it once in Hudu if it doesn't exist yet).

claude._comment: Cost/quality controls for the classifier/resolver pipeline (see CLAUDE.md). 'effort' is the fallback default applied to the classifier and every resolver call whenever a more specific effort setting below is blank. Lowered from 'medium' to 'low' on 2026-09-02 as a cost lever - the classifier/resolver's own tool-call loop, not raw thinking depth, was driving most of the token spend, so this trades some depth for a meaningful per-call discount. 'classifier_effort'/'resolver_effort_trivial'/'resolver_effort_medium'/'resolver_effort_complex' (v2.10.10) are per-call overrides, blank any of them out to fall back to plain 'effort' above instead of a specific value (no separate 'resolver_effort_approved' - the APPROVED tier reuses resolver_model_trivial's model, so it reuses resolver_effort_trivial too). resolver_effort_medium/resolver_effort_complex raised from 'low' back to 'medium' on 2026-09-07 - those two tiers are the genuinely agentic, multi-tool-investigation work (unlike the classifier's structured JSON output, where effort barely matters), and low effort risks under-investigating exactly the tickets that need real depth. classifier_model/resolver_model_trivial switched from Haiku 4.5 to Sonnet 5 on 2026-09-17 (Roger's own call, not a bug fix) - every tier now runs Sonnet 5, with effort scaled to match each tier's actual complexity (classifier_effort/resolver_effort_trivial 'low', resolver_effort_medium 'medium', resolver_effort_complex raised to 'high' the same day) rather than varying by model choice. On 2026-09-25 all four resolver tiers were set to 'medium' (Roger's call): one effort level also means one shared prompt cache, since Claude Code keys its cache by effort level. classifier_effort stays 'low'. This also means every tier's configured effort value is now actually sent - Haiku 4.5 never accepted --effort at all (the CLI would reject it), which is why resolver_effort_trivial/classifier_effort used to be documented as having no effect; that caveat no longer applies now that both run on Sonnet 5. 'classifier_effort' also covers the one-time-per-cycle ID resolution call, which always runs on classifier_model. IMPORTANT: not every model accepts --effort at all - Invoke-HaloResponseAgent.ps1 only ever sends --effort when the model actually being called is on its own confirmed-supported allowlist ($effortCapableModels - current Sonnet/Opus tiers only), silently omitting it otherwise so an unsupported model is never sent a value it would reject; -DryRun's output shows exactly what would/wouldn't be sent. resolver_model_* is chosen per ticket by the tier the classifier assigned it - TRIVIAL_UNCERTAIN uses resolver_model_trivial too, since that path just asks for missing info and stops rather than investigating. Compare a few -WhatIf runs' WOULD DO quality at 'low' against 'medium'/'high' before trusting a lower value live - see README's 'Reducing per-run cost' section. id_cache_max_age_hours: how long the Halo team/status/priority/agent ID cache (agent-cache.json) stays valid before a cycle re-resolves it fresh, even if halo.* below hasn't changed - a backstop for the rare case where Halo itself changes (a team renamed, an agent account recreated) without this file changing. Lower it if that happens more than rarely at your MSP; the cache also invalidates itself immediately, with no need to wait out this window, any time you edit a name in the halo section below. blocked_ticket_retry_hours (v2.10.30) controls how long a ticket stays excluded from the classifier's candidate list after the resolver reports it via [CACHE: BLOCKED] - a structural dead end (Halo's own untriaged-ticket write-swallow bug, a genuine agent-permissions gap) that a human has to fix in Halo itself, where retrying immediately next cycle would just reproduce the identical failure at the identical cost. Real incident: one such ticket cost over a dollar across three consecutive cycles in about ten minutes with no sign it would ever stop reprocessing on its own, since the underlying problem (no write lands at all, not even the tracking note) meant the classifier never saw evidence anything had already been tried. After this many hours the ticket simply becomes a normal candidate again - long enough that a human has a real chance to have fixed it, short enough that a fix doesn't sit unnoticed for a full day. human_owned_retry_hours (v2.10.60) is the same cooldown shape as blocked_ticket_retry_hours, for a different cause: how long a ticket stays excluded from the classifier's Unassigned candidate list after the resolver reports it via [CACHE: HUMAN_OWNED] - a real human agent already confirmed (via the ticket's own action log, not just its current status/assignment) to be working the ticket by hand. Real incident: tickets #22114/#22067 were each reprocessed 6 times in one day at Sonnet-tier cost, every single pass correctly re-discovering 'a human already owns this' the expensive way, because a human's habit of resetting a ticket's status back to New while working it (which also clears agent_id back to 1) makes it indistinguishable from a genuinely fresh candidate to every cheaper signal the classifier has. Defaulted considerably longer than blocked_ticket_retry_hours (24h here vs. 2h there) since the two situations aren't symmetric: a platform bug might get fixed within the hour and is worth re-checking soon, but a human actively working a ticket by hand isn't in a hurry to hand it back, and ready_for_ai_status_name already exists as the correct, immediate way to signal 'actually, take this one' regardless of this cooldown - lower it if your team's real workflow means tickets bounce back to this pipeline sooner than a day. max_remembered_notes (v2.10.44) caps agent-cache.json's remembered_notes list - durable notes a human explicitly asked the agent to keep in mind for future tickets (see resolver-prompt.md's 'Remembering something for future tickets'), injected into every resolver call. Unlike blocked_ticket_retry_hours above, entries here never age out on their own (they're meant to be permanent institutional knowledge, not a transient retry state) - this cap is the only thing bounding the list's growth, oldest entries dropped first once it's exceeded, so the resolver prompt's size (and therefore every future call's cost) doesn't grow without bound as more gets remembered over time.

pipeline._comment: Feature flags for the cost/speed program (v2.11.0+). Every flag defaults to false, and a missing key or missing block means false, so a deployment that never adds this block behaves exactly as before. This file is never auto-synced from the repo, so turning a flag on (or back off) here is the whole rollout and the whole rollback for that change - no code push involved. Turn one on only after Replay-Tickets.ps1 shows it holds up on real tickets (see README's 'Replay evaluation' section). deterministic_classifier (increment 2, v2.12.0): PowerShell asks halopsa-mcp's /helpdesk-triage route for every candidate bucket (the classifier prompt's calls 1-6 as plain Halo REST calls), applies the mechanical exclusions itself, and makes ONE no-tool tiering call (rules read live from classifier-prompt.md) only if any candidate needs a tier - falls back to the LLM classifier for that cycle if anything fails. classifier_shadow (v2.12.0): rollout aid - with deterministic_classifier off, still run the deterministic path every cycle and log a CLASSIFIER SHADOW COMPARISON section (both answers per ticket, agreement count, both costs) while the LLM's answer is the one used; turn shadow on first, watch a day of logs, then turn deterministic_classifier on and shadow off. skip_status_names (v2.12.0): status names the deterministic path treats as an active workflow this pipeline can't act on (dropped from the unassigned bucket, never applied to ready_for_ai_status_name); a trailing * is a prefix match; the default list mirrors the examples in classifier-prompt.md - edit it to match this tenant's statuses. prefetch_ticket (increment 3): the same brief, recent history, contact and device data are injected into the resolver prompt up front so it doesn't spend its first several tool calls re-fetching them. prefetch_history / prefetch_max_note_chars / prefetch_max_details_chars / prefetch_max_chars (v2.14.1, defaults 25 / 2000 / 6000 / 40000): how much ticket that block carries - it is re-read on every resolver turn, so a smaller block is the lever if prefetching cuts turns but not cost; the resolver can still call get_ticket_history for anything beyond it. client_reply_style (v2.15.8): "detailed" (default, today's replies) or "brief" - the investigation and internal note are unchanged, but the client-facing reply is two to four plain, non-technical sentences; missing details are still asked for plainly, security sign-in alerts and the forwarded-email reminder keep their current wording, and anything that needs a person gets a holding reply (initial diagnostics done, a technician will follow up) with the full findings in the internal note. Set back to "detailed" to return to today's replies; no code push either way. duplicate_guard (v2.15.0, the one flag that defaults ON - a missing key means on): a new unassigned ticket whose contact (Halo user, the ticket's email, or an 'Email:' line in a web-form body) already has an OLDER ticket waiting for approval is held instead of investigated - one private note naming the earlier ticket, no model call, left for a person to merge; the hold lifts once the earlier ticket leaves AI Waiting Approval, and Ready for AI overrides it. duplicate_guard_ignore_domains: email domains that never count as a matching contact (your own staff, who open and forward tickets for many clients). playbooks (increment 4): a lean core resolver prompt plus per-topic playbooks (network, email, VPN, security, approval flows) selected per ticket, instead of the whole document every time. client_cards (increment 5): a small cached context card per client (network vendor, VLAN map, servers, known quirks - built from Hudu and live lookups, re-verified on use) injected only for that client's tickets.

remediation_whitelist.name: Reset M365 password
remediation_whitelist.requires: Ticket contact's email matches the target account's login exactly.

remediation_whitelist.name: Unlock M365 account
remediation_whitelist.requires: Account confirmed to belong to the ticket contact.

remediation_whitelist.name: Reboot workstation
remediation_whitelist.requires: Device belongs to the ticket contact, is not a server, and the user has been told a reboot is happening.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Reset Printing
remediation_whitelist.requires: Print-related issue only. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Clear Print jobs and restart spooler
remediation_whitelist.requires: Print-related issue only. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Flush DNS
remediation_whitelist.requires: Network connectivity issue only (can't reach a specific site/service), device not a server. Mac/Linux. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Clear DNS cache
remediation_whitelist.requires: Network connectivity issue only (can't reach a specific site/service), device not a server. Windows. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Release & Renew IP Address
remediation_whitelist.requires: Network connectivity issue only, device not a server. Windows. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Delete Temporary Files
remediation_whitelist.requires: Disk-space or general slowness complaint only, device not a server. Windows. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Windows Update Reset
remediation_whitelist.requires: Windows Update stuck, failing, or erroring only. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: SFC Scannow
remediation_whitelist.requires: Windows system-file corruption suspected (crashes, missing/corrupt system files, erratic OS behavior not explained by anything else), device not a server. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Run Windows Cleanup
remediation_whitelist.requires: Disk-space or general slowness complaint, device not a server. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: gpupdate /force
remediation_whitelist.requires: Group Policy hasn't applied / a policy-managed setting isn't taking effect, device not a server. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Latest Wrike Desktop Install
remediation_whitelist.requires: The client asked for Wrike to be updated, upgraded, or allowed to update on their computer (any wording: 'allow the Wrike update', 'Wrike says a new version is available', 'update Wrike'). Windows workstation, not a server, identified via the ticket's device hints or a NinjaOne device lookup (hostname or last-logged-in-user match). Wrike must already be installed on that device - confirm with mcp__Ninja__get_device_software (look for 'Wrike for Windows') before running; if it is not installed this is a new-software request for a human, not an update. Run it with mcp__Ninja__run_script_and_wait, tell the client the update was applied and to restart Wrike (it is safe to run while Wrike is open, but they may need to relaunch it), and record the before/after version in the internal note. Script name must match exactly what's in NinjaOne.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Enable Remote Desktop Service
remediation_whitelist.requires: Device belongs to the ticket contact (not a shared/kiosk device) and they've explicitly asked for remote access to their own machine. This is a persistent access change - nothing disables it automatically - so log clearly in the internal note that RDP was enabled and why.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Add <Company Abbreviation> VPN Configuration
remediation_whitelist.requires: Windows workstation only, confirmed via a NinjaOne device lookup (hostname or last-logged-in-user match) to belong to the ticket contact - not a shared/kiosk device, not a guess. The script is per-client, always named 'Add <abbreviation> VPN Configuration' (e.g. 'Add Gold VPN Configuration' for Gold Mechanical, Inc.) - find the one whose abbreviation actually matches this ticket's client via mcp__Ninja__list_automation_scripts, don't assume the exact name. VPN client software must not already be present on the device (check first) - don't re-run it if it's already installed. Not OpenVPN in any form; Altec is moving away from it.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run NinjaOne script: Speedtest (JSON)
remediation_whitelist.requires: User/client states they are having network speed issues, performance issues that could be related or vague, and network issues.

remediation_whitelist.name: Run Meraki throughput test
remediation_whitelist.requires: Client reports slow network/internet performance and their firewall is confirmed to be a Meraki MX/Z-series appliance (via Hudu's network-stack asset or a live mcp__Meraki__ lookup - see resolver-prompt.md's network section, never assumed). Diagnostic, not a fix - tests WAN throughput at the firewall itself, for isolating whether slowness is upstream of the client's own network versus local to one workstation. Use mcp__Meraki__run_throughput_test, which already waits for and returns the result.

remediation_whitelist.name: Sign a user out of all sessions
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__CIPP__revoke_user_sessions (tenantFilter, ID = the user's UPN). Only when the account is confirmed to belong to the ticket contact (or the person the ticket is about, at the same client) AND either they ask for it (lost or stolen device, signed in somewhere they shouldn't be) or a security alert/sign-in check shows a session that should be ended. Never for an admin, service or shared account - that needs a person. Tell the user they will have to sign in again on every device.

remediation_whitelist.name: Add a user to a group
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__CIPP__add_group_member (tenantFilter, GroupId, UserId). Only when someone at the client explicitly asks in the ticket for this user to get access that a specific group provides (a shared mailbox, distribution list, Team or SharePoint site), naming the user and the access - never inferred. Confirm the group exists in that tenant with mcp__CIPP__list_groups and that the user is not already a member. Never an admin-role, security or Conditional Access group (anything granting admin rights or changing sign-in policy) - those need a person.

remediation_whitelist.name: Remove a user from a group
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__CIPP__remove_group_member (tenantFilter, GroupId, UserId). Only when someone at the client explicitly asks in the ticket to remove this user's access that a specific group provides, naming the user and the access. Confirm membership first with mcp__CIPP__list_group_members. Never an admin-role, security or Conditional Access group, and never remove a group's last owner - those need a person.

remediation_whitelist.name: Set an out-of-office reply
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__CIPP__set_mailbox_ooo (tenantFilter, userId, AutoReplyState Enabled/Disabled/Scheduled, InternalMessage, ExternalMessage). Only when the mailbox owner, or their manager at the same client, asks for it in the ticket. Use the message they gave, word for word; if they gave none, ask for it rather than writing one. Use Scheduled only when they gave dates. Turning it off (Disabled) on request is always fine.

remediation_whitelist.name: Assign or remove a license
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__CIPP__set_user_license (tenantFilter, UserId, AddLicenses / RemoveLicenses as SKU IDs from mcp__CIPP__list_licenses). Only when someone at the client explicitly asks in the ticket, naming the user and the license. To assign, confirm with mcp__CIPP__list_licenses that an unused license of that type is available - never buy or add licenses; if none is free, say so and hand to a person. Never remove a license unless asked to, and never remove the last license from an active user's account without that explicit request.

remediation_whitelist.name: Convert a mailbox to shared
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__CIPP__convert_mailbox (tenantFilter, userId, MailboxType Shared). Only Regular to Shared, only for a departing or departed user, and only when someone at the client asks for it in the ticket (typically an offboarding). Confirm the account is the one named. Never convert an active user's mailbox, and never Shared to Regular - that needs a person.

remediation_whitelist.name: Acknowledge or resolve a NinjaOne alert
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__Ninja__acknowledge_alert or mcp__Ninja__resolve_alert (alert_uid from mcp__Ninja__list_device_alerts). Only for an alert on a device in this ticket, and resolve only when you've confirmed the condition behind it is cleared (disk space freed, service running again, device back online). Never resolve an alert to hide a problem that is still happening.

remediation_whitelist.name: Approve or reject a pending OS patch
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__Ninja__approve_os_patch or mcp__Ninja__reject_os_patch (device_id, patch_id from mcp__Ninja__get_device_os_patches). One patch on one device in this ticket at a time, never in bulk. Approve when the client's problem is that a needed update isn't installing and the patch is waiting for approval. Reject only when this specific patch is confirmed (cited source) to cause the problem reported. Policy-wide patch decisions need a person.

remediation_whitelist.name: Put a device in maintenance mode or end it
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__Ninja__set_device_maintenance (device_id, end, optional start) or mcp__Ninja__end_device_maintenance (device_id). Only for a device in this ticket when the ticket says it will be offline or worked on (a move, a repair, a planned shutdown), so its alerts don't page anyone. End time no more than 24 hours out unless the ticket gives a longer window. End maintenance as soon as the ticket says the work is done.

remediation_whitelist.name: Reboot a Meraki access point or switch
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__Meraki__reboot_device (serial). Access points and switches only, never the security appliance/firewall (MX or Z series) - that takes the whole site offline and needs a person. Only when the device is confirmed in this client's network and confirmed misbehaving (offline, alerting, clients failing to connect through it). Tell the client the area it serves will drop for a few minutes; during business hours only unless it's already down.

remediation_whitelist.name: Turn a switch port off and on again
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__Meraki__update_switch_port (serial, portId, enabled false, then enabled true). Only on an access port confirmed to serve the affected device (matched by the device's MAC/IP in mcp__Meraki__list_network_clients or the port's own details), never an uplink or trunk, or a port to another switch, the firewall or a server. Record the port's settings before and after in the findings note.

remediation_whitelist.name: Change a switch port's VLAN
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__Meraki__update_switch_port (serial, portId, vlan). Only on an access port confirmed to serve the affected device, when its IP or VLAN is confirmed wrong for that device (checked against mcp__Meraki__list_vlans and how matching devices' ports are set, or the client's Hudu network docs), and the correct VLAN is clear from that evidence. Never a trunk or uplink port. Record the old and new VLAN in the findings note.

remediation_whitelist.name: Change a Wi-Fi network's settings
remediation_whitelist.requires: Use mcp__Meraki__update_ssid (networkId, number, and only the fields being changed). Only when someone at the client explicitly asks in the ticket for a specific change to a named Wi-Fi network: its name, turning it on or off, or a new password they supplied in the ticket (never invent one). Never change the security/authentication type - that needs a person. Record the old values in the findings note and tell the client every device on that network will need to reconnect.
